headline: Ryan Day: a life and a career
card_headline: Ryan Day: a life and a career
hero_caption: Ryan Day, head coach, Ohio State University.
standfirst: Ryan Day has been the head coach at Ohio State since 2019. He grew up in Manchester, New Hampshire, played quarterback at the University of New Hampshire, and worked at four schools and two NFL teams before he got there. What follows is that career, set out in order, along with the Week 3 power rankings of the Chach Champions League.
shrine_title: The life and career of Ryan Day
shrine_sub: Set down here in the order it happened.

timeline.text: Born March 12 in Manchester, New Hampshire.
Quarterback at Manchester Central High School. Named New Hampshire's Gatorade player of the year.
Quarterback at the University of New Hampshire. Team captain as a senior. His offensive coordinator was Chip Kelly.
First coaching job, tight ends at New Hampshire.
Graduate assistant at Boston College, then at Florida.
Five seasons coaching wide receivers at Boston College.
Offensive coordinator at Temple, then offensive coordinator and quarterbacks at Boston College.
Quarterbacks coach in the NFL, first with the Philadelphia Eagles, then with the San Francisco 49ers alongside Chip Kelly again.
Hired at Ohio State as co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Acting head coach for the first three games of the season. Ohio State won all three.
First full season as head coach. The team finished 13-1.
Won the national championship, beating Notre Dame 34-23.
Beat Michigan 27-9, ending a four-game losing run in the rivalry.
Ohio State is 3-1 through four games, the loss by a single point at Texas. Most recently a 42-19 win over Illinois on September 26.

takes.2: Ben's Brilliant Team scored 150.84 and beat michael's Monstrous Team by 3.88, the closest game of the week. Jaxon Smith-Njigba led the way with 35.4. The receivers, the tight end and the kicker each finished first in the league at their position, which is the first time any team has done that this season. Three wins from three. Ryan Day was born on March 12, 1979, in Manchester, New Hampshire.
takes.3: CeeDeez Nutz scored 133.64 and beat Adams and Jefferson by 43.64. Christian Watson led the team with 22.6 from the flex, and the Vikings defense added 19, the best defensive figure of the week. The team is 3-0 and second in the rankings, having won every week without once holding the highest score. Day played quarterback at Manchester Central High School and was named New Hampshire's Gatorade player of the year.
takes.9: michael's Monstrous Team scored 146.96, the highest losing score recorded this season, and lost by 3.88. Jahmyr Gibbs returned 41.4, the best individual figure in the league this week. A further 107.54 points were left on the bench, more than seven teams scored in total. The team falls from first to third at 2-1. Day played quarterback at the University of New Hampshire from 1998 to 2001 and was a captain in his senior year.
takes.7: Purdy Seconds to Mars scored 149.08 against 65.92, a margin of 83.16 and the widest of the season so far. Bijan Robinson led the team with 35.3. It is a second consecutive win and lifts the team two places to fourth at 2-1. Day's offensive coordinator at New Hampshire was Chip Kelly, who later hired him twice in the NFL.
takes.4: Cortisol Spyke Weeks scored 139.44 and beat Team Galakrond by 48.3. Ja'Marr Chase led the team with 24.8, and both the backfield and the receiver room finished in the league's top three. It is a second straight win and a rise of five places to fifth, the largest move anybody made this week. Day's first coaching job came in 2002, with the tight ends at New Hampshire.
takes.8: Dake Bates scored 96.48 and beat the roadrunners by 5.14 in the lowest-scoring game of the week. Jordan Love led the team with 18.5. It was the lowest winning score on the board, and the team sits sixth at 2-1, having opened the season with 177.86 in week one. Day spent 2003 and 2004 as a graduate assistant at Boston College, then 2005 in the same role at Florida.
takes.6: Bingo Night scored 65.92 and lost by 83.16. Travis Kelce led the team with 13.9. The bench returned 82.8, well above the lineup that played, and the team lost all eleven of its all-play matchups, the first time any team has done so this season. The record stands at 2-1, seventh in the rankings. Day coached wide receivers at Temple in 2006.
takes.12: Team evil scored 109.08 and beat Drake Maye Sucks Ass by 14.32 for its first win of the season. Garrett Wilson led the team with 26.7. The 49ers defense returned nothing. The team rises three places to eighth at 1-2, after losing by 75.9 in week one and by 0.4 in week two. Day coached wide receivers at Boston College for five seasons, from 2007 to 2011.
takes.5: Adams and Jefferson scored 90.00 and lost by 43.64. Matthew Stafford led the team with 20.9. A further 81.54 points were left on the bench. The team is 0-3 while holding the fourth-most points in the league, a combination no other team has managed this season. Day was offensive coordinator at Temple in 2012, then at Boston College in 2013 and 2014.
takes.11: Drake Maye Sucks Ass scored 94.76 and lost by 14.32. Drake London led the team with 28.4. Drake Maye, the quarterback the team is named after, returned 3.8, and the Eagles defense finished at minus one, a negative figure in a starting lineup. The team falls two places to tenth at 1-2. Day coached quarterbacks in the NFL for two seasons, with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2015 and the San Francisco 49ers in 2016.
takes.1: Team Galakrond scored 91.14 and lost by 48.3. Kenneth Walker led the team with 21.3 and the backfield produced 40.4, the best rushing figure of the week. Every other position returned less than the league average. The team is 0-3 and eleventh. Day arrived at Ohio State in 2017 as co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and served as acting head coach for the first three games of 2018, all of which the team won.
takes.10: The roadrunners scored 91.34 and lost by 5.14. Matthew Golden led the team with 21.0, and the tight end slot returned zero for the second time in three weeks. A further 72.18 points were left on the bench. The team is 0-3 and twelfth, the only side yet to record a win or a top-half finish. Day's first full season as head coach, in 2019, ended 13-1, and Ohio State won the national championship in January 2025, beating Notre Dame 34-23.
